summary: Complete contributor map of the primary loopback Studio, its separately gated remote listeners, and its source-preview terminal companion. Kit terminal shell covers composition, discovery, sessions, providers, documentation and capability tools, staged review, and responsive presentation. Folder-derived apps, setup, context menus, and in-app docs define extension points. Infrastructure includes development reload, provenance chips, storage, receipts, and HTTP routes, including revision-checked editor writes and host-only remote-access and update families. Library owns importing and staging and visibly reports damaged files without changing them; Workbench owns persistent editors and split panes; Press owns staged export runs with explicit unknown-loss reporting when a target has no coverage declaration. Settings derives Appearance, Studio, Workbench, Remote access, Updates, and About from modules. Shared components centralize color and paint controls. Security distinguishes the primary loopback listener from opt-in remote boundaries while retaining fail-closed parsing, scripts-as-data, and sanitized app marks.

sections.title: Kit terminal shell
sections.summary: Kit is a source-checkout terminal preview with a multiline composer, paste cards, bounded follow-up queue, draft-preserving history and search, interruptible streaming, command palette, studio-piece mentions, and context-sensitive suggestions. Native scrolling, foldable long replies, copy feedback, responsive rainbow branding, and a session-local stage watcher keep terminal behavior coherent. Atomic sessions support resume, rewind, fork, and export. Model settings, doctor checks, inventory, and privacy are command surfaces. Its tool loop performs bounded studio and documentation reads, discovers only a small deferred capability set, composes previews, and replaces model save prose with a revision-checked REVIEW CHANGE gate. Applies and discards serialize, receipts retain lifecycle truth in Backstage, provider preambles stay out of the user transcript, and explicit stop reasons expose budget or progress limits.

sections.title: Hyper-modularity (the build's spine)
sections.summary: UI applications are drop-in folders exporting a HoplightApp manifest and component. Bun discovery skips private underscore folders, bundles apps on demand, puts ordinary apps on the Dock, and keeps catalogOnly tools available through the catalog without a central roster. Apps receive AppContext and may reach engine or filesystem behavior only through its API; the shell owns global navigation, tabs, theme, and status. Visual law comes from one token sheet rather than app-local colors or fixed layout. Bright accents remain marks, borders, and spines; any labeled accent fill uses a generated deep companion with stage-white text. Rose, house accent, deck, and per-piece pairs share tested deepening logic.

sections.title: First-run setup (the wizard)
sections.summary: First run is assembled from drop-in SetupStep folders, each declaring its question, options, settings key, optional widget and stage treatment, and recap language. The wizard derives order, progress, defaults, skipping, stage zones, and final summary from discovery; pure selection and sentence logic is tested separately. Settings are an open record parsed fail-closed per known key and persisted under the studio directory. Missing setupComplete opens the wizard; completion applies theme and house accent and follows the manifest-selected first landing, while later starts choose the lowest-order app. Theme changes use View Transitions when appropriate, retain an immediate reduced-motion fallback, persist server-side, and use localStorage only for pre-paint. Serialized PATCH operations ensure concurrent control changes merge rather than overwrite stale documents.

sections.title: The right-click system
sections.summary: One shared context-menu service grows through registration. Surfaces attach typed targets and data to elements, with the deepest matching element winning and a shell-level target always available. Features register any number of item providers for a target type; each provider contributes a section, an empty result denies by absence, and cleanup receives an unregister function. Shell providers currently cover entity actions such as send, show, open beside, split close, and Workbench removal, plus Dock-app and shell navigation actions. A new feature contributes one provider instead of editing a central switch, preserving room-independent behavior for common entity operations.

sections.title: Apps catalog and documentation
sections.summary: The Dock's Add app control discovers the manifest-marked catalog instead of naming an id, and the catalog derives cards from the running app roster. catalogOnly tools such as CSS Workshop and Help/Docs remain bundled without occupying everyday Dock space. Help/Docs reads the committed corpus through the generated docs index, which can merge frontmatter, semantic page summaries, retrieval topics, and nested section anchors. Navigation separates user workflows and platforms from developer API, architecture, data, format, security, extension, and decision material; ADR filenames remain canonical while titles are reader-friendly. Markdown uses the shared sanitizer, figures and images are restricted to generated or committed docs assets, the right rail follows current headings, and packaged content matches GitHub. External GitHub viewing passes through the leaving gate and URL allowlist.

sections.title: Dev live-reload
sections.summary: Development Studio watches src/ui and broadcasts changes to every open page over the /dev/reload server-sent-event stream. Browser bundles are rebuilt per request, so a save produces fresh code instead of a cached build. Packaged executables serve baked assets, return 404 for the development stream, and let the client become quiet without a separate dependency.

sections.title: The card-type chip
sections.summary: Library summaries derive sourceFormat and sourceVariant from the first non-Hoplight escrow record. Labels come from the live format registry rather than a duplicated UI map: platform-specific adapters show platform and variant, generic Tavern/CC content shows Default, and pieces authored without a source adapter display no chip. The badge therefore describes provenance without inventing one for native drafts.

sections.title: The studio store
sections.summary: Canonical Hoplight JSON is the local database: each entity lives at studioDir/kind/id.json as a portable file. Storage never replaces a different piece at the same id; it creates a numbered sibling, enforcing Keep both at persistence. One inventory pass returns healthy summaries and separate bounded records for safe-id JSON files that fail parsing, canonical schema, kind, or id checks. Damaged files are never modified or quarantined.

sections.title: The receipt
sections.summary: The server renders one plain-language import receipt for both shells, ensuring terminal and visual users receive the same explanation. It uses recognizable platform names, a we-read/we-kept voice, and emits conditional lines only when engine evidence supports embedded books, scripts-as-data, or privileged warnings. Unknown files receive a warm failure message. Receipt rendering adds presentation, not new detection or format logic.

sections.title: Endpoints
sections.summary: The HTTP surface serves the shell, token sheet, boot code, discovered app manifests and bundles, and setup-step modules. Settings supports read, replacement, and validated partial merge. Documentation routes expose the generated index, figures, catalog-declared Markdown, and committed assets. Formats, inspect, export, coverage, and Studio routes remain thin engine and storage boundaries. `/api/studio/inventory` returns healthy entities and bounded damaged-file records from one filesystem scan; `/api/studio/list` remains the healthy-only compatibility read. Editor reads can return the complete entity with its revision, and editor saves atomically compare that revision, returning 409 without overwriting newer data. Bundle saves validate the complete canonical batch before any write, then report genuine storage partials honestly. Host-only `/api/remote/*` routes control tunnel and LAN setup, devices, and approvals; `/api/updates/*` routes read release information and perform version switching.

sections.title: The Library room (the shelves - deep browse)
sections.summary: Library presents first-run doors when empty and, when populated, live per-kind deck counts, a drop-in proscenium view, portrait-backed covers, drop-anywhere import receipts, and the configured initial deck. It loads healthy summaries and damaged records together through one `/api/studio/inventory` filesystem pass and renders an expandable notice even when no readable pieces remain. The notice names each file and bounded reason, states that Hoplight did not change it, includes the local studio path when available, and offers manual restore-or-remove guidance. Grid, showcase, and list are DeckView modules behind the one browser registry seam; each receives consistent open and staged states. Tapping ordinary pieces toggles a staging set that survives deck switches, then sendMany moves the batch through one follow decision reporting the true newly opened count. Already-open pieces remain annotation-only, while the context menu preserves one-shot Send. A continuous, fail-closed 4-to-36rem art-size control updates CSS live and persists on release. View choice and size live in per-user Library preferences.
topics: drop-in grid showcase and list views

sections.title: The Workbench room (home by default - the IDE)
sections.summary: Workbench is the shell-owned tabbed IDE for character, lorebook, persona, preset, regex, and pack entities; editors retain local drafts and save explicitly. Each editor loads a complete-entity revision and saves only against that revision, so an external write leaves the draft dirty and reports a conflict instead of being overwritten. One shared editor-guard hook publishes dirty state, owns Ctrl+S and window-close protection, and routes tab, keyboard, editor-back, and context-menu closes through a shell-owned discard-or-keep dialog. send and sendMany share ask/always/never follow behavior, while create and open-beside gestures navigate directly. Recents combines import and open times, excludes current tabs, caps history, and can collapse. Character editing preserves untouched body fields, persistent prose order, dirty state, and variant semantics shared with Kit operations. Split view supports any two kinds with tested focus, promotion, and close rules. Pane container queries, not viewport queries, drive responsive collapse. Lorebook editing centers one entry with searchable groups, trigger modes, timing, placement, passage, platform-specific cards, fine controls, match testing, and honest token estimates. The shell also persists a marks-only Dock mode.

sections.title: The Press room (batch export - the staged set prints)
sections.summary: Press exports only a shell-owned staged queue assembled from Library or its unstaged-piece rail, so queue state survives app switches and the room does not duplicate a studio browser. Characters automatically gather referenced lorebooks from the whole studio; riders may be dropped for one run, and an already staged riding book is not exported twice. Readiness compares characters with the target's live field-coverage claims and identifies lorebook entries that cannot fire, offering editor repair links without manufacturing green status when claims are absent. Export reports preserve that distinction: undeclared coverage is unknown with a null dropped count rather than false zero loss. Each run chooses one grouped platform target, declares filenames, text flavors, and skips before work, reports printed, skipped, or failed outcomes per row, and emits one zip. Delivery history, saved jobs, reorder, byte rehearsal, and readiness dots remain explicitly deferred.

sections.title: Settings (drop-in sections)
sections.summary: Settings tabs derive from section modules exporting id, label, order, and a component that receives AppContext. The section registry is the sole browser seam, so adding configuration does not require a central tab switch. Controls operate against current persisted settings and immediately repaint visual choices. Shipping sections are Appearance for theme and accent, Studio for home app, initial deck, and publish targets, Workbench for follow behavior, Remote access for tunnel and LAN setup, devices, and host controls, Updates for release checks and version switching, and About.

sections.title: Shared components (`src/ui/_shared/` and `src/ui/components/`)
sections.summary: Shared visual controls are extracted once for setup, settings, and future editors. SwatchRow exposes the house palette as quick choices and optionally opens PaintPicker for a custom solid color. ColorPicker provides a branded saturation/value square, hue strip, and hex input while retaining HSV internally to avoid grayscale-state loss. Pure color math normalizes and converts values fail-closed and shares pointer fractions across color and gradient controls. The Paint model is a validated discriminated union for solid, linear, and radial output; gradients require at least two valid stops. PaintPicker composes color editing, stop add/drag/remove, angle adjustment, and curved previews behind allowed-mode gates. Solid accent use is live; tested gradient editing awaits its first entity or pack background consumer.

sections.title: Security
sections.summary: The primary Studio listener binds loopback. Optional remote listeners are separate, explicitly enabled boundaries with join secrets, device approval, and host-only controls. Uploads use the CLI engine's fail-closed format parsers and archive-expansion limits rather than a permissive UI parser. Scripts stored inside entities remain data throughout Studio workflows. Third-party manifest SVG marks are sanitized before Dock or catalog insertion, removing scripts, foreignObject content, and event handlers.
